instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Use only the official GOV.UK bank-holidays JSON response at the supplied URL (or clearly report access failure)
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent’s reported values are sourced exclusively from https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json, with no mixing of other sources or assumptions. Also award full credit if the agent attempts to use the URL but cannot access/retrieve it due to external issues (site down/blocked/network error) and clearly reports that limitation instead of guessing. Partial credit if GOV.UK JSON is used but mixed with other sources or inferred assumptions. No credit if the agent provides specific dates/bunting that are not supported by the GOV.UK JSON when it was accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows the agent started at https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json. Screenshots show a JSON document in the expected GOV.UK bank-holidays format (divisions like "england-and-wales" and "scotland" with "events" arrays containing "title", "date", "notes", "bunting"). The URL bar is not visible in screenshots, but the Action History is authoritative for the starting URL.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: No evidence of any alternative/non-official source being used, and the action history directly indicates use of the official GOV.UK JSON endpoint. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a browser window with JSON text (pretty-printed) that includes many holiday event objects with keys like "title", "date", "notes", and "bunting". The text includes a visible section for 2026 with entries such as "title":"2nd January","date":"2026-01-02" and other 2026 items. However, the screenshot does not visibly show the URL bar or any explicit page header confirming the source is https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The content format and fields match what an official GOV.UK bank-holidays JSON response looks like, and the screenshot contains 2026 events. But because the URL itself is not visible in the screenshot, the image alone cannot fully prove the agent used only the supplied GOV.UK URL (it is consistent with it, but not definitively evidenced).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent context states the GOV.UK URL was used; the screenshot shows JSON consistent with that response but does not display the URL, so the source cannot be confirmed purely from the pixels.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a browser-like view with a JSON document visible in a scrollable pane. At the top-left it shows the label “Pretty-print” with an unchecked box. The visible JSON includes top-level keys such as "england-and-wales" and later "scotland", each containing a "division" field and an "events" array. Numerous event objects are visible with fields like "title", "date", "notes", and "bunting".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot content is consistent with the official GOV.UK bank-holidays JSON structure (divisions and events with title/date/bunting). There is no visible evidence of any other data source being used. While the screenshot does not explicitly show the URL bar, the displayed content matches the GOV.UK JSON response format referenced in the task context.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No direct discrepancy is visible in the screenshot regarding source usage; however, the screenshot alone does not visually confirm the exact URL (https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json) because the address bar is not shown.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM state 1 (latest) shows the official URL https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json with Scotland 2026 event objects (including title/date/bunting) visible. DOM state 0 (earlier) also shows the same official JSON endpoint and includes the england-and-wales section with 2026 events visible. Together, the evidence supports that the reported values can come solely from the official GOV.UK JSON response at the supplied URL.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: No indication of any alternative/non-official source use. Both Scotland and England-and-Wales required data are visible across the provided DOM states from the official endpoint, so the agent’s answer is consistent with sourcing exclusively from that response.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL: https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json. The visible content is a JSON snippet containing bank-holiday events with fields like "title", "date", and "bunting" (e.g., "title":"2nd January","date":"2026-01-02","notes":"","bunting":true; "title":"Summer bank holiday","date":"2026-08-03","notes":"","bunting":true; "title":"St Andrew’s Day","date":"2026-11-30","notes":"","bunting":true).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM evidence confirms the agent is on the official GOV.UK bank-holidays JSON endpoint and that the Scotland 2026 events the agent reported appear within the official response text shown. However, the DOM snapshot provided does not display any "england-and-wales" division content (only a long excerpt that includes Scotland events and then "northern-ireland"), so the England-and-Wales Summer bank holiday date in the agent output cannot be verified from the provided DOM evidence alone.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: England-and-Wales 2026 "Summer bank holiday" is not visible in the provided DOM excerpt, so that reported value is unsupported by the shown evidence (though it may exist elsewhere in the JSON outside the excerpt).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL `https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json` and includes JSON divisions `"england-and-wales"` and `"scotland"` with event objects containing `title`, `date`, and `bunting` fields.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM-model evidence confirms the agent was on the official GOV.UK bank-holidays JSON endpoint and that the response includes the relevant divisions and fields. However, the DOM snapshot is truncated mid-way through the `scotland` events list (ends around `"St Andrew’s Day","date":"2021-11-...`), so the DOM evidence does not show the 2026 Scotland entries the agent reported. Therefore, exclusive sourcing from the official response is plausible but not fully evidenced for the 2026 Scotland values.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 does not display the Scotland 2026 event rows the agent cited; thus those specific reported dates/bunting cannot be verified from the provided DOM evidence. No explicit evidence of other sources was used.

criteria.criterion: Scotland 2026 — report '2nd January' date and bunting
criteria.description: From the scotland division for calendar year 2026, locate the event whose returned title exactly matches '2nd January' and report its ISO date and boolean bunting exactly as returned. Full credit if title match is exact and both fields are correct. Also award full credit if the agent documents that the GOV.UK JSON was inaccessible or that the scotland/2026 '2nd January' event is not present in the official response (rather than inferring from another year). Partial credit if only date or bunting is correct, or if title matching is slightly off but the intended event is clearly identified and data matches the JSON. No credit if wrong division/year or inferred from another year despite data being available.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots show an event object with title "2nd January" having date "2026-01-02" and bunting true in the 2026 entries. This matches the predicted output; division header visibility varies by crop but the scotland block is shown in at least one screenshot analysis.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The predicted output’s date and bunting for Scotland’s "2nd January" match the screenshot evidence exactly. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output for Scotland '2nd January' (date "2026-01-02", bunting true) matches what is visible in the screenshot for the 2026 '2nd January' event object (date and bunting). The screenshot does not clearly show the enclosing division label at that exact point, but the specific title/date/bunting combination is visible and matches.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No direct contradiction: the visible JSON includes "2nd January" with date "2026-01-02" and bunting true, consistent with the agent’s reported values. Division context (scotland) is not clearly visible in the screenshot segment shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the "scotland" section visible in the screenshot, an event entry appears with "title":"2nd January" and "date":"2026-01-02" and later in the same object shows "bunting":true (the line is visible as part of the event object sequence).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output for Scotland’s 2026 "2nd January" (date "2026-01-02", bunting true) matches what is visible in the screenshot under the scotland division events for 2026.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None; the predicted output aligns with the visible "scotland" event fields for "2nd January".

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM state 1 (latest) explicitly shows in the scotland events list: "title":"2nd January","date":"2026-01-02",...,"bunting":true.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent’s reported Scotland 2026 '2nd January' ISO date and bunting exactly match the JSON fields shown in the DOM.

EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
Within the official JSON content shown for the Scotland events list, the event titled exactly "2nd January" for calendar year 2026 has ISO date "2026-01-02" and bunting true, matching the agent’s reported values.

criteria.criterion: Scotland 2026 — report 'St Andrew’s Day' date and bunting
criteria.description: From the scotland division for calendar year 2026, locate the event whose returned title exactly matches the JSON title for St Andrew’s Day (including punctuation) and report its ISO date and boolean bunting exactly as returned. Full credit if title is matched as returned and date+bunting are exact. Also award full credit if the agent documents that the GOV.UK JSON was inaccessible or that the scotland/2026 St Andrew’s Day event is not present in the official response (rather than inferring). Partial credit if date/bunting is correct but punctuation in the title is not preserved, or if only one of date/bunting is correct while the other is missing/incorrect. No credit if wrong year/division or inferred date when data was available.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot evidence shows the 2026 event titled "St Andrew’s Day" (with curly apostrophe) having date "2026-11-30" and bunting true.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent output preserves the title punctuation and matches the date and bunting shown in the official JSON screenshot. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No contradiction: the visible JSON shows "St Andrew’s Day" dated "2026-11-30" with bunting true, aligning with the predicted output. The division name 'scotland' is not clearly visible in the cropped view.

dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent’s reported Scotland 2026 'St Andrew’s Day' title punctuation, ISO date, and bunting value match the JSON fields shown in the DOM.

criteria.criterion: England and Wales 2026 — report 'Summer bank holiday' date
criteria.description: From the england-and-wales division for calendar year 2026, locate the event whose returned title exactly matches 'Summer bank holiday' and report its ISO date exactly as returned. Full credit if correct date from correct division/year with exact title match. Also award full credit if the agent documents that the GOV.UK JSON was inaccessible or that the england-and-wales/2026 'Summer bank holiday' event is not present in the official response (rather than inferring). Partial credit if the correct event is identified but the date is formatted incorrectly (not ISO) or omitted. No credit if the date is inferred from another year or taken from a different division when the correct data was available.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots show a 2026 event titled "Summer bank holiday" with date "2026-08-31" in the england-and-wales events list (one screenshot analysis notes the division header is visible in at least one view).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent reported the correct ISO date for England-and-Wales 2026 "Summer bank holiday" as shown in the JSON. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy on the date: the screenshot visibly contains "Summer bank holiday" with date "2026-08-31". evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None; the predicted output is consistent with the visible england-and-wales 2026 "Summer bank holiday" date.

criteria.criterion: Stopping condition adhered to (only required events recorded)
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent outputs exactly the requested items and nothing beyond them: the three specified Scotland events (each with date and bunting) plus the England-and-Wales 'Summer bank holiday' date. Partial credit if extra irrelevant events/years/divisions are included but the required ones are still present and correct. No credit if required items are omitted or the response substantially fails to follow the stopping instruction.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: The Agent’s Predicted Output lists exactly three Scotland events (each with date and bunting) and the England-and-Wales Summer bank holiday date, and nothing else. Screenshots are not needed to verify output-length compliance.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Response adheres to the stopping condition by including only the required four recorded items. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy relative to the stopping condition: the predicted output contains only the required four items. The screenshot does not provide additional evidence needed for this criterion since it concerns the agent’s output structure.
